description: Use free browser tools to convert Philippine coordinates and inspect GeoJSON data. Start a practical mapping task without signing in.
heading: Free geospatial tools
intro: Small, practical utilities for coordinates and map data. Choose a task and start in your browser; no account is required.

title: Luzon 1911 Coordinate Converter | Spatialdom
description: Convert Luzon 1911 longitude and latitude to Philippine Transverse Mercator grid coordinates, or convert PTM X and Y back. Choose a zone and copy the result.
heading: Luzon 1911 coordinate converter
intro: Enter Luzon 1911 longitude and latitude, or PTM X and Y, then choose the correct Philippine zone. Results update as you type.
howToUse: Choose Geo to Grid or Grid to Geo, then select the Luzon 1911 zone used by your source data.
Enter longitude and latitude in decimal degrees or DMS, or enter PTM X and PTM Y. Copy the compact or detailed result.
meaning: PTM X and Y are projected grid coordinates in meters. Longitude and latitude are angular coordinates. The zone and datum must match the source; otherwise a plausible looking result can still be misplaced.
This converter works with Luzon 1911 geographic and grid coordinates. It is not a WGS 84 latitude/longitude to UTM converter, and it does not establish a legal parcel boundary.

insight.label: Read about coordinate systems and zones

title: View GeoJSON Online | Spatialdom
description: Open a GeoJSON file in your browser, check its features and geometry types, and inspect properties on an interactive map. No account required.
heading: GeoJSON viewer
intro: Choose a .geojson or .json file to check its structure, inspect features, and view them on a map. The file is read in your browser.
howToUse: Choose or drop a GeoJSON file. The viewer checks its structure and reports the feature count and geometry types.
Explore the map, tap a feature to inspect its properties, or use Zoom to Extents to return to your data.
meaning: GeoJSON describes features such as points, lines, and polygons with coordinates and optional properties. Standard GeoJSON uses WGS 84 longitude and latitude in that order.
The viewer reads the selected file locally in your browser. Map tiles are requested from the selected basemap provider; your GeoJSON file is not uploaded by this tool.
